articles.title: Rockstar Games gets a taste of grand theft data amid ShinyHunters threat of 'Pay or leak'
articles.summary: Rockstar Games is facing an extortion attempt by the threat actor ShinyHunters, who is threatening to leak sensitive data unless their financial demands are met. This incident highlights a significant data security breach targeting the gaming industry.

articles.title: Alleged German DDoS-for-Hire Kingpin Behind Fluxstress Caught in Thailand
articles.summary: A German individual suspected of operating the Fluxstress and Neldowner DDoS-for-hire services has been arrested in Thailand after a long-running investigation. The arrest marks the dismantling of a significant global cybercrime infrastructure used for launching distributed denial-of-service attacks.

articles.title: Siemens expands Industrial Automation DataCenter with edge AI and cybersecurity
articles.summary: Siemens is upgrading its Industrial Automation DataCenter with NVIDIA AI technology and integrated cybersecurity solutions provided by Palo Alto Networks. This partnership aims to enhance edge computing capabilities while bolstering security for industrial production environments.

articles.title: Adobe issues emergency fix for Acrobat Reader flaw exploited in the wild (CVE-2026-34621)
articles.summary: Adobe released an emergency patch for a critical zero-day prototype pollution vulnerability (CVE-2026-34621) in Acrobat Reader that has been actively exploited since November 2025. The flaw allows for arbitrary code execution in the context of the user, provided the attacker has local access.

articles.title: Seized VerifTools servers expose 915,655 fake IDs, 8 arrested
articles.summary: Dutch authorities arrested eight suspects and seized servers belonging to the identity fraud platform VerifTools, which contained over 915,000 fake IDs. The operation targeted users and operators involved in large-scale forgery and cybercriminal activity.

articles.title: NHS pays £46K to prep next Microsoft licensing round
articles.summary: The NHS is allocating £46,000 to prepare for an upcoming renewal of its Microsoft software licensing agreements. This administrative action ensures continued access to enterprise tools and security updates.

articles.title: North Korea's APT37 Uses Facebook Social Engineering to Deliver RokRAT Malware
articles.summary: The North Korean threat group APT37 is utilizing social engineering on Facebook to build rapport with targets and deliver the RokRAT remote access trojan. This multi-stage campaign demonstrates a shift toward leveraging trusted social platforms for malware distribution.

articles.title: Iran-linked group Handala claims to have breached three major UAE organizations
articles.summary: An Iran-linked threat group named Handala claims to have breached three major Dubai government organizations, allegedly destroying 6 petabytes of data and exfiltrating 149 terabytes.

articles.title: CPUID watering hole attack spreads STX RAT malware
articles.summary: Threat actors compromised the official CPUID website to distribute STX RAT malware by replacing legitimate CPU-Z and HWMonitor installers with malicious versions. The attack successfully provided attackers with remote access to the systems of users who downloaded the tampered files.

articles.title: Fixing vulnerability data quality requires fixing the architecture first
articles.summary: Art Manion argues that the inconsistency in vulnerability data stems from fundamental architectural flaws in how systems manage and collect such information. The research highlights the difficulty in establishing a universal standard, such as Minimum Viable Vulnerability Enumeration, due to the contextual nature of vulnerabilities.

articles.title: ZeroID: Open-source identity platform for autonomous AI agents
articles.summary: ZeroID is an open-source identity and credentialing platform designed to solve the attribution problem in autonomous and multi-agent systems by providing traceability for agent actions. It addresses the security limitations of shared service accounts and traditional OAuth protocols in complex agentic workflows.

articles.title: MITRE releases a shared fraud-cyber framework built from real attack data
articles.summary: MITRE has introduced the Fight Fraud Framework (F3) to bridge the operational gap between fraud investigators and cybersecurity analysts by providing a unified, behavior-based model for identifying and responding to financial attacks.

articles.title: Bringing governance and visibility to machine and AI identities
articles.summary: AppViewX CEO Archit Lohokare discusses the growing need for unified governance and visibility for machine and AI identities as autonomous systems increasingly replace human-driven processes. The company is addressing this shift by integrating certificate lifecycle management, PKI, and agentic governance to secure emerging digital identity frameworks.

articles.title: China wants AI to prepare school lessons and mark homework
articles.summary: China is planning to integrate artificial intelligence into its educational system to assist with lesson planning and grading student assignments. This initiative reflects a growing trend in the state-led adoption of AI technology across public sectors.

articles.title: Anthropic's mysterious Mythos AI threatens to upend the infosec world
articles.summary: The emergence of Anthropic's 'Mythos' AI model suggests potential disruptions in the cybersecurity landscape, raising concerns about its capability to impact industry practices. The report highlights speculative risks regarding how such advanced AI could alter the threat landscape.

articles.title: The fully free Linux OS Trisquel gets a major update with version 12.0 Ecne
articles.summary: Trisquel GNU/Linux has released version 12.0, codenamed Ecne, featuring updates to the kernel, packaging, and the integration of APT 3.0. This production-ready update aims to enhance the security and repository management for home, enterprise, and educational users.

articles.title: Adobe fixes actively exploited Acrobat Reader flaw CVE-2026-34621
articles.summary: Adobe has released emergency updates to address a critical, actively exploited vulnerability in Acrobat Reader that could allow attackers to execute malicious code. The flaw, identified as CVE-2026-34621, carries a CVSS score of 8.6.

articles.title: Hacker Used Claude Code, GPT-4.1 to Exfiltrate Hundreds of Millions of Mexican Records
articles.summary: A lone actor utilized AI tools, specifically Claude Code and GPT-4.1, to exfiltrate hundreds of millions of personal records from nine Mexican government agencies. This incident highlights the growing risk of AI-assisted cyberattacks on critical public sector infrastructure.

articles.title: Critical Marimo pre-auth RCE flaw now under active exploitation
articles.summary: A critical pre-authentication remote code execution vulnerability in Marimo is currently being actively exploited to steal credentials. Users should patch immediately to prevent unauthorized access and data compromise.

articles.title: Hackers claim control over Venice San Marco anti-flood pumps
articles.summary: Hackers have allegedly breached Venice's San Marco flood control system, gaining the ability to manipulate pumps and disable critical defensive infrastructure. The incident highlights the growing risks associated with the security of operational technology (OT) in essential infrastructure.

articles.title: SECURITY AFFAIRS MALWARE NEWSLETTER ROUND 92
articles.summary: The Security Affairs newsletter provides an analysis of recent malware campaigns, including malicious npm packages targeting Strapi, Kimsuky's evolving LNK distribution methods, and exploitation of ComfyUI servers.

articles.title: FBI Atlanta and Indonesian National Police Take Down W3LLSTORE Phishing Marketplace
articles.summary: The FBI and Indonesian National Police have dismantled the W3LLSTORE phishing marketplace, which was associated with $20 million in fraud, leading to domain seizures and the arrest of its lead developer.

articles.title: Security Affairs newsletter Round 572 by Pierluigi Paganini – INTERNATIONAL EDITION
articles.summary: The 572nd edition of the Security Affairs newsletter reports on Censys findings regarding thousands of devices exposed to Iranian APTs and developments concerning the GlassWorm malware.

articles.title: Week in review: Windows zero-day exploit leaked, Patch Tuesday forecast
articles.summary: This weekly review highlights the leak of a Windows zero-day exploit and upcoming Patch Tuesday expectations, alongside Cloudflare's updated roadmap for post-quantum security readiness.

articles.title: Adobe Patches Actively Exploited Acrobat Reader Flaw CVE-2026-34621
articles.summary: Adobe has released an emergency patch for a critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-34621) in Acrobat Reader that is currently being exploited in the wild. The flaw could allow attackers to execute arbitrary code on vulnerable systems.

articles.title: Censys finds 5,219 devices exposed to attacks by Iranian APTs, majority in U.S.
articles.summary: Censys has identified over 5,000 internet-exposed Rockwell Automation PLCs in the U.S. that are being actively targeted by Iranian-linked threat actors. Agencies including the FBI, CISA, and NSA have issued warnings to critical infrastructure operators to secure these devices immediately.

articles.title: GlassWorm evolves with Zig dropper to infect multiple developer tools
articles.summary: The GlassWorm campaign has evolved to use Zig-based droppers disguised as IDE extensions to conduct supply chain attacks and deploy RATs across developer platforms. The operation targets various developer tools, marking a significant escalation in its ongoing malicious activity.

articles.title: FBI Recovers Deleted Signal Messages Through iPhone Notifications
articles.summary: Court documents reveal that the FBI can access deleted Signal messages by extracting data from iPhone notification logs. This highlights a persistent privacy risk where message content cached by the iOS notification system remains retrievable despite in-app deletion.

articles.title: Over 20,000 crypto fraud victims identified in international crackdown
articles.summary: An international law enforcement operation spearheaded by the U.K.'s National Crime Agency has uncovered a major cryptocurrency fraud scheme affecting over 20,000 individuals across the U.K., U.S., and Canada.

articles.title: Google Chrome Update Disrupts Infostealer Cookie Theft
articles.summary: Google has introduced Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC) in Chrome 146, a new security feature that ties session cookies to hardware keys to prevent infostealers from hijacking user sessions on Windows.

articles.title: Two different attackers poisoned popular open source tools - and showed us the future of supply chain compromise
articles.summary: Recent incidents involving the poisoning of popular open-source tools highlight an evolving trend in supply chain attacks, demonstrating how threat actors are increasingly targeting software dependencies to gain widespread unauthorized access. These events underscore the urgent need for enhanced security measures within the open-source ecosystem to prevent systemic compromise.

articles.title: CVE-2026-39987: Marimo RCE exploited in hours after disclosure
articles.summary: The open-source Python tool Marimo suffered a critical remote code execution vulnerability, CVE-2026-39987, which was actively exploited in the wild within 10 hours of its disclosure. The flaw carries a CVSS score of 9.3, indicating a severe risk to affected systems.

articles.title: Hungarian government creds left in the safe hands of 'FrankLampard'
articles.summary: Hungarian government credentials were found exposed online, reportedly secured by an account using the alias 'FrankLampard'. This indicates a significant security lapse involving sensitive administrative access.

articles.summary: OpenAI has introduced a new $100 Pro subscription tier for ChatGPT, aligning its pricing strategy more closely with competitor Claude. This move signals heightened market competition in the enterprise AI space.

articles.title: ShinyHunters Claims Rockstar Games Snowflake Breach via Anodot
articles.summary: The threat actor ShinyHunters claims to have accessed Rockstar Games' data through a third-party breach of Anodot, threatening a data leak if ransom demands remain unmet. The incident highlights potential supply chain vulnerabilities involving Snowflake environments.

articles.title: Android Banking Trojan Linked to Cambodia Scam Compounds Hits 21 Countries
articles.summary: An Android banking trojan connected to forced labor scam operations in Cambodia is actively targeting users across 21 countries to steal funds by bypassing security measures. This campaign highlights the intersection of organized criminal human trafficking and sophisticated cybercrime operations.

articles.title: Commerce setting up new AI export regime to push adoption of ‘American AI’ abroad
articles.summary: The U.S. Department of Commerce is developing a framework to promote and export American-made artificial intelligence technology to international allies. This initiative aims to strengthen global adoption of U.S.-aligned AI standards and systems.

articles.title: Senator launches inquiry into 8 tech giants for failures to adequately report CSAM
articles.summary: A U.S. Senator has initiated an inquiry into eight major technology companies following allegations from the NCMEC regarding their failure to properly report child sexual abuse material (CSAM) and manage data concerns related to generative AI.

articles.title: UK government threatens tech bosses with jail time if they do not adequately fight nudification tools
articles.summary: The UK government is threatening tech executives with imprisonment if they fail to implement measures to stop the proliferation of non-consensual AI-generated nudification tools. This crackdown follows the recent Grok scandal, which facilitated the global circulation of deepfake imagery targeting women and children.

articles.title: ‘It reads like a spy novel’: $280 million theft from Drift involved North Korean fake companies, cutouts
articles.summary: The $280 million theft from Drift was orchestrated by North Korean actors who infiltrated the company by posing as a quantitative trading firm at a cryptocurrency conference. This sophisticated social engineering operation highlights the persistence and methods of state-sponsored threat actors in targeting financial infrastructure.

articles.title: GraphAlgo Scam: Lazarus Hackers Register Real US LLCs to Spread Malware
articles.summary: The North Korean Lazarus group is leveraging legitimate US-based LLCs and GitHub typo-squatting to distribute malware through the GraphAlgo campaign, specifically targeting software developers. This sophisticated technique bypasses traditional trust markers by utilizing registered corporate identities to facilitate cyberattacks.

articles.title: Nearly 4,000 US industrial devices exposed to Iranian cyberattacks
articles.summary: Approximately 4,000 internet-exposed Rockwell Automation industrial controllers in the U.S. have been identified as potential targets for Iranian-linked cyberattacks. These devices represent a significant risk to critical infrastructure networks.

articles.title: Ransomware attack on ChipSoft knocks EHR services offline across hospitals in the Netherlands and Belgium
articles.summary: A ransomware attack on healthcare IT provider ChipSoft has forced its HiX electronic health record platform offline, causing widespread service disruptions across hospitals in the Netherlands and Belgium.

articles.title: Florida investigates OpenAI for role ChatGPT may have played in deadly shooting
articles.summary: Florida authorities are investigating OpenAI after a family alleged that the gunman involved in a deadly shooting used ChatGPT extensively in the period leading up to the attack. The family plans to pursue legal action against the company regarding the AI's potential influence.

articles.title: Analysis of one billion CISA KEV remediation records exposes limits of human-scale security
articles.summary: An analysis of one billion CISA KEV records reveals that current human-driven patching processes cannot keep pace with the speed at which attackers exploit critical vulnerabilities. The study highlights a systemic failure in remediation timelines, suggesting that automated security measures are becoming essential for effective defense.

articles.title: ClickFix campaign delivers Mac malware via fake Apple page
articles.summary: Security researchers have identified a ClickFix social engineering campaign that tricks Mac users into executing malicious commands under the guise of disk maintenance. The attack utilizes a deceptive Apple-themed webpage to compromise systems.

articles.title: GlassWorm Campaign Uses Zig Dropper to Infect Multiple Developer IDEs
articles.summary: The GlassWorm campaign has evolved to use a Zig-based dropper hidden within a malicious Open VSX extension to compromise developer IDEs. This supply chain attack targets development environments by masquerading as legitimate productivity software.

articles.title: Supply chain attack at CPUID pushes malware with CPU-Z/HWMonitor
articles.summary: Threat actors compromised the CPUID project's API to replace legitimate download links for CPU-Z and HWMonitor with malicious versions. This supply chain attack poses a significant risk to users who downloaded the tools during the period of compromise.

articles.title: UK says it exposed Russian submarine activity near undersea cables
articles.summary: The UK Ministry of Defence reported that Russian naval assets, including an attack submarine and research vessels, were monitored engaging in suspicious activities near critical undersea infrastructure. This disclosure highlights growing concerns over potential sabotage risks to international subsea communication cables.

articles.title: CPUID site hijacked to serve malware instead of HWMonitor downloads
articles.summary: The official CPUID website was compromised to distribute malicious software disguised as legitimate HWMonitor downloads. Users who downloaded the software during the incident were likely infected with malware.

articles.title: UNC6783 Hackers Use Fake Okta Pages in Corporate Breach Campaign
articles.summary: The UNC6783 threat group is conducting a corporate breach campaign by using social engineering and fraudulent Okta login pages to impersonate support staff and exfiltrate sensitive data.

articles.title: Microsoft: Canadian employees targeted in payroll pirate attacks
articles.summary: A threat actor identified as Storm-2755 is targeting Canadian employees by hijacking payroll accounts to steal salary payments. Microsoft is actively tracking these financially motivated attacks.

articles.title: Poisoned “Office 365” search results lead to stolen paychecks
articles.summary: A threat actor identified as Storm-2755 is using SEO poisoning, malvertising, and AiTM phishing to hijack employee payroll accounts. By mimicking Office 365, the group tricks victims into redirecting their salary payments to attacker-controlled bank accounts.

articles.title: Project Glasswing and open source software: The good, the bad, and the ugly
articles.summary: This headline explores the implications of Project Glasswing, an initiative potentially related to AI or open-source supply chain security, examining both its advantages and risks within the ecosystem.

articles.title: UAT-10362 linked to LucidRook attacks targeting Taiwan-based institutions
articles.summary: The threat group UAT-10362 is targeting NGOs and universities in Taiwan using a new Lua-based malware dubbed LucidRook, distributed through password-protected phishing emails.

articles.title: Britain seeks views before it drops the hammer on signal jammers
articles.summary: The British government is initiating a consultation period to gather public and industry feedback before implementing stricter regulations and enforcement against the illegal use of signal jammers. This move aims to curb the unauthorized disruption of telecommunications services across the country.

articles.title: Browser Extensions Are the New AI Consumption Channel That No One Is Talking About
articles.summary: The rise of AI-powered browser extensions presents an overlooked security vulnerability, as these tools often operate without sufficient oversight or enterprise protection. LayerX reports that these extensions constitute a significant, unguarded threat surface within corporate networks.

articles.title: Google rolls out Gmail end-to-end encryption on mobile devices
articles.summary: Google has expanded its end-to-end encryption (E2EE) features for Gmail to all Android and iOS mobile devices for enterprise users. This update allows organizations to secure their communications natively without requiring third-party tools.

articles.title: Gmail’s end-to-end encryption comes to mobile, no extra apps required
articles.summary: Google has extended end-to-end encryption to the Gmail mobile app for Enterprise Plus users, allowing for secure handling of sensitive data without requiring third-party applications. This update improves mobile security and helps organizations maintain compliance with data sovereignty requirements.

articles.title: To counter cookie theft, Chrome ships device-bound session credentials
articles.summary: Google has introduced Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC) in Chrome to prevent session hijacking by linking authentication cookies to specific devices. This security measure aims to mitigate the effectiveness of infostealer malware that targets and exfiltrates browser cookies.

articles.title: EngageLab SDK flaw opens door to private data on 50M Android devices
articles.summary: A critical vulnerability in the EngageLab SDK allows malicious applications to bypass Android sandbox protections and access sensitive user data, impacting approximately 50 million devices including numerous crypto wallets.

articles.title: Little Snitch for Linux shows what your apps are connecting to
articles.summary: Objective Development has released a free Linux version of its popular Little Snitch firewall, providing desktop users with visual, per-process monitoring of outbound network connections using eBPF technology.

articles.title: Apiiro CLI turns AI coding assistants into full-stack security engineers
articles.summary: Apiiro has launched a new CLI tool that integrates its security platform directly into AI coding assistants, providing developers with automated risk management, remediation, and threat modeling capabilities. This integration aims to transform AI coding tools into full-stack security assistants by embedding native security analysis workflows.

articles.title: Unpacking AI security in 2026 from experimentation to the agentic era
articles.summary: This article explores the evolution of AI security in 2026, focusing on the shift from initial AI experimentation toward managing the risks associated with increasingly autonomous agentic systems.

articles.title: Google Rolls Out DBSC in Chrome 146 to Block Session Theft on Windows
articles.summary: Google has launched Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC) for Windows Chrome users to prevent session hijacking and token theft. This feature securely binds authentication sessions to a specific device, effectively mitigating risks from stolen session cookies.

articles.title: Marimo RCE Flaw CVE-2026-39987 Exploited Within 10 Hours of Disclosure
articles.summary: A critical pre-authenticated remote code execution vulnerability, CVE-2026-39987, in the open-source Marimo data science platform was exploited within ten hours of its public disclosure.

articles.title: April 2026 Patch Tuesday forecast: Spring-cleaning of a preview
articles.summary: The article previews the upcoming April 2026 Patch Tuesday updates while reflecting on the growing integration of AI into security products and industry discourse.

articles.title: Bitcoin Depot hack leads to $3.6M Bitcoin theft via stolen credentials
articles.summary: Bitcoin Depot, the largest US Bitcoin ATM operator, suffered a security breach on March 23 in which hackers stole credentials and drained approximately 50.9 BTC, valued at $3.6 million, from company wallets.

articles.title: Backdoored Smart Slider 3 Pro Update Distributed via Compromised Nextend Servers
articles.summary: Threat actors compromised Nextend's update servers to distribute a backdoored version of the Smart Slider 3 Pro plugin. This supply chain attack affects users who updated to version 3.5.1.35.

articles.title: What vibe hunting gets right about AI threat hunting, and where it breaks down
articles.summary: This article discusses 'vibe hunting,' an AI-driven approach to threat detection that shifts focus from pre-defined hypothesis-based hunting to identifying anomalous patterns. It emphasizes the need for human analysts to maintain explainability and oversight to prevent over-reliance on AI decision-making.

articles.title: Health insurance lead sites sell personal data within seconds of form submission
articles.summary: Researchers discovered that health insurance lead generation websites rapidly sell users' sensitive personal data to multiple third-party buyers immediately after form submission. This study highlights significant privacy risks and the aggressive monetization of consumer information by lead generation platforms.

articles.title: Product showcase: Session, a messenger without phone numbers or metadata
articles.summary: Session is an instant messaging platform that enhances user privacy by eliminating the need for phone numbers and minimizing metadata collection. It focuses on secure communication through end-to-end encryption, addressing growing concerns regarding data surveillance.

articles.summary: Dutch healthcare software provider ChipSoft experienced a ransomware attack, leading to the disruption of digital services used by hospitals and patients throughout the Netherlands.

articles.title: New ‘LucidRook’ malware used in targeted attacks on NGOs, universities
articles.summary: A novel Lua-based malware named 'LucidRook' is being deployed in targeted spear-phishing campaigns against NGOs and universities in Taiwan.

articles.title: New VENOM phishing attacks steal senior executives' Microsoft logins
articles.summary: A new phishing-as-a-service platform called VENOM is being used to target and steal Microsoft login credentials from C-suite executives across various industries.

articles.title: Iranian attacks on US critical infrastructure puts 3,900 devices in crosshairs
articles.summary: Censys researchers identified approximately 3,900 internet-exposed devices at risk of exploitation by Iranian-backed actors targeting critical U.S. infrastructure. The campaign specifically focuses on the energy, water, and government services sectors.

articles.title: Why is the timeline to quantum-proof everything constantly shrinking?
articles.summary: Rapid advancements in quantum computing and geopolitical concerns are accelerating the urgency for organizations to transition to post-quantum cryptography. Experts warn that the window for securing sensitive data against future quantum-enabled decryption is closing faster than anticipated.

articles.title: Eurail data breach impacted 308,777 people
articles.summary: Eurail suffered a data breach in December 2025, resulting in the theft of personal information, including names and passport numbers, for 308,777 travelers. The company is currently notifying affected individuals regarding potential identity theft risks.

articles.title: FCC proposes new rule to further crackdown on illegal robocalls
articles.summary: The FCC has proposed a new regulation requiring originating service providers to verify customer data and implement stricter oversight to combat illegal robocalls. Non-compliant providers face increased financial penalties for failing to block these malicious communications on their networks.

articles.title: Healthcare IT solutions provider ChipSoft hit by ransomware attack
articles.summary: Dutch healthcare software provider ChipSoft experienced a ransomware attack, forcing the company to take its patient and provider-facing digital services offline. The incident highlights the ongoing threat of ransomware targeting critical infrastructure within the healthcare sector.

articles.title: Malicious PDF reveals active Adobe Reader zero-day in the wild
articles.summary: Cybersecurity researcher Haifei Li has discovered a malicious PDF file exploiting an actively used Adobe Reader zero-day vulnerability that has been leveraged by hackers for several months. The researcher is currently seeking assistance from the security community to conduct a full analysis of the exploit.

articles.title: Google Chrome adds infostealer protection against session cookie theft
articles.summary: Google has introduced Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC) in Chrome 146 for Windows to prevent info-stealing malware from hijacking session cookies. This security feature binds session cookies to the user's specific device, significantly mitigating the impact of session theft attacks.

articles.summary: A now-patched security vulnerability in the EngageLab Android SDK allowed apps to bypass the system's security sandbox, exposing sensitive data for 50 million users including 30 million crypto wallets.

articles.title: Treasury Department announces crypto industry cyber threat sharing initiative
articles.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department has launched an initiative to provide qualified digital asset firms with access to the same cybersecurity threat intelligence currently shared with traditional financial institutions. This move aims to bolster the defense of the cryptocurrency industry against emerging cyber threats.

articles.summary: Hackers are actively exploiting an unpatched zero-day vulnerability in Adobe Reader through malicious PDFs to steal data without requiring user interaction. Due to the lack of an available patch, the threat poses a significant risk to organizations and individuals.

articles.title: UAT-10362 Targets Taiwanese NGOs with LucidRook Malware in Spear-Phishing Campaigns
articles.summary: A newly identified threat actor group, UAT-10362, is conducting spear-phishing campaigns against Taiwanese NGOs and universities to deliver a novel Lua-based malware called LucidRook. articles.title: Smart Slider updates hijacked to push malicious WordPress, Joomla versions
articles.summary: Hackers compromised the update server for the Smart Slider 3 Pro plugin, distributing malicious updates containing backdoors to WordPress and Joomla websites. This supply chain attack poses a significant threat to sites using the plugin.

articles.title: Inside the FBI’s router takedown that cut off APT28’s ‘tremendous access’
articles.summary: The FBI successfully neutralized a Russian GRU-linked APT28 campaign that utilized compromised routers to gain widespread access to target networks. This operation disrupted the sophisticated capabilities of the threat actor to propagate malicious activity beyond initial router access points.

articles.title: Chevin pulls the handbrake on FleetWave software after security scare
articles.summary: Chevin has suspended access to its FleetWave software following a security concern to prevent potential unauthorized access or data exposure. The company is currently investigating the incident to ensure the integrity of its platform.

articles.summary: The Russian FSB has accused a former Radio Free Europe journalist of providing intelligence to the Ukrainian Security Service to facilitate cyberattacks. articles.title: Claude Managed Agents bring execution and control to AI agent workflows
articles.summary: Anthropic has launched Claude Managed Agents, a suite of APIs designed to provide secure, sandboxed infrastructure and management for deploying scalable AI agent workflows. articles.summary: Threat actors are exploiting a months-old zero-day vulnerability in Adobe Reader through malicious PDF files to perform reconnaissance on targeted systems. The attack leverages existing security flaws to profile environments before potentially deploying further payloads.

articles.summary: The AI girlfriend platform MyLovely.AI suffered a data breach exposing over 113,000 users' emails, NSFW prompts, and linked social media accounts. This incident highlights significant privacy risks associated with AI-driven interactive platforms.

articles.summary: Masjesu is a stealthy DDoS-for-hire botnet that has been targeting IoT devices since 2023 by strategically avoiding high-profile networks to maintain persistence. The botnet leverages cross-architecture support to compromise routers and gateways for malicious infrastructure.

articles.title: When attackers already have the keys, MFA is just another door to open
articles.summary: The headline highlights that traditional MFA is vulnerable to session hijacking and phishing, necessitating a shift toward device-bound biometric authentication to verify the user rather than the session. This approach addresses the limitation where attackers use stolen credentials to bypass conventional MFA methods.

articles.summary: Microsoft has blocked developer accounts associated with VeraCrypt and WireGuard, citing issues with their identity verification process. This incident has raised concerns about the impact of rigid corporate security policies on open-source project maintenance.

articles.summary: This bulletin covers a diverse range of security threats, including a hybrid P2P botnet and a 13-year-old Apache remote code execution vulnerability being exploited. The report highlights persistent risks from overlooked legacy flaws and the exploitation of trusted platforms.

articles.summary: This webinar explores how to identify early warning signs of cyberattacks, such as dark web activity and credential listings, to enable proactive defense. It focuses on converting raw threat intelligence into actionable security measures.

articles.summary: Cryptocurrency ATM operator Bitcoin Depot reported a cyberattack resulting in a $3.6 million loss after unauthorized actors compromised credentials linked to its digital asset settlement accounts.

articles.summary: Bryan Fleming, the creator of the pcTattleTale stalkerware app, received a sentence of a fine and supervised release after pleading guilty to charges related to his software. This case marks a rare instance of a successful U.S. prosecution against a stalkerware developer.

articles.summary: Cloudflare has introduced EmDash, an AI-powered CMS platform designed to address inherent WordPress security vulnerabilities through sandboxed plugins, serverless scaling, and passkey authentication.

articles.summary: The shift toward multi-OS cyberattacks highlights the risks of fragmented security operations across diverse enterprise environments. articles.summary: Proton has released an open-source, end-to-end encrypted 2FA app that supports cross-platform synchronization and privacy-focused features. It enables users to secure accounts with TOTP codes without tracking or advertisements.

articles.summary: LinkedIn is under scrutiny for allegedly tracking over 6,000 browser extensions installed on users' computers, sparking significant privacy and data surveillance concerns. The report, dubbed 'BrowserGate,' highlights potential unauthorized data collection practices.

articles.summary: Senator Ron Wyden has cautioned the Social Security Administration against participating in a Trump administration executive order, alleging the creation of a voter database facilitates voter suppression.
